# Lab 15.11: Redact & Pseudonymize PII

## What We Are Going to Do
Call the Sensitive Data Protection API to redact, mask and pseudonymize text, then reverse the pseudonymization with the same key.

## Steps

1. **Set a token variable and the API URL.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">export TOKEN=$(gcloud auth print-access-token)
export DLP=https://dlp.googleapis.com/v2/projects/$PROJECT_ID/locations/global</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **Replace values with their infoType.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">curl -s -X POST "$DLP/content:deidentify" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{
  "item": {"value": "Call Asha on 415-555-0100 or asha@example.com"},
  "inspectConfig": {"infoTypes": [{"name": "PHONE_NUMBER"}, {"name": "EMAIL_ADDRESS"}]},
  "deidentifyConfig": {"infoTypeTransformations": {"transformations": [
    {"primitiveTransformation": {"replaceWithInfoTypeConfig": {}}}]}}
}' | grep value</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   Result: `Call Asha on [PHONE_NUMBER] or [EMAIL_ADDRESS]`.

3. **Mask instead.** Change the transformation to:


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • JSON
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">{"primitiveTransformation": {"characterMaskConfig": {"maskingCharacter": "#"}}}</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   Result: `Call Asha on ############ or #################`.

4. **Create a lab key for pseudonymization.** In production this key is wrapped by Cloud KMS (`kmsWrapped`). An unwrapped key is only for learning.


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">export KEY=$(openssl rand -base64 32)</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


5. **Pseudonymize the email.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">curl -s -X POST "$DLP/content:deidentify" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{
  "item": {"value": "Customer asha@example.com placed an order"},
  "inspectConfig": {"infoTypes": [{"name": "EMAIL_ADDRESS"}]},
  "deidentifyConfig": {"infoTypeTransformations": {"transformations": [
    {"primitiveTransformation": {"cryptoDeterministicConfig": {
      "cryptoKey": {"unwrapped": {"key": "'"$KEY"'"}},
      "surrogateInfoType": {"name": "EMAIL_TOKEN"}}}}]}}
}' | grep value</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   Result: `Customer EMAIL_TOKEN(52):AXk... placed an order`. Run it twice: the token is the same each time.

6. **Re-identify it.** Paste the full output text into `TOKENIZED_TEXT`.


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">curl -s -X POST "$DLP/content:reidentify" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{
  "item": {"value": "TOKENIZED_TEXT"},
  "inspectConfig": {"customInfoTypes": [{"infoType": {"name": "EMAIL_TOKEN"}, "surrogateType": {}}]},
  "reidentifyConfig": {"infoTypeTransformations": {"transformations": [
    {"infoTypes": [{"name": "EMAIL_TOKEN"}],
     "primitiveTransformation": {"cryptoDeterministicConfig": {
      "cryptoKey": {"unwrapped": {"key": "'"$KEY"'"}},
      "surrogateInfoType": {"name": "EMAIL_TOKEN"}}}}]}}
}' | grep value</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   The original email comes back.

7. **Save it as a template.** In **Sensitive Data Protection → Configuration → Templates**, create a **De-identify template** with the same transformation, so pipelines reuse it.

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Replace with infoType | Readable, data removed |
| Masking | Characters replaced, irreversible |
| Deterministic encryption | Same input, same token, reversible with the key |
| Production key | Wrapped with Cloud KMS, never unwrapped |
